recent_posts.title: Distinguishing between human and programmatic scrolling
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to distinguish between human and programmatic scrolling in JavaScript by using the 'wheel' event. The post demonstrates how to implement automatic scrolling while allowing the user to take control when they scroll manually. It introduces the ResizeObserver and shows a practical implementation of managing auto-scroll behavior in a chat simulation.

recent_posts.title: Animate streaming text with a one-line hook
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to build a React hook for animating streaming text. The guide covers smoothing out text responses, handling new incoming chunks, pausing, and restarting animations. It uses the framer-motion library for rich animations and demonstrates integrating the hook into a production application for real-time text display.

recent_posts.title: Building a Reusable Component that Animates on Scroll
recent_posts.summary: Learn to build a reusable, animated 'Fade up' component using React and Framer Motion. This component animates elements as they come into the viewport while offering customization options like delays and animation styles. The guide covers turning divs into motion components, using hooks to manage state, and applying animations that persist as elements scroll in and out of view. Perfect for adding interactive animations to your web projects.

recent_posts.title: Avoid premature abstraction with Unstyled Components
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to avoid premature abstraction in React by using unstyled components. This approach helps in sharing logic like loading spinners without enforcing styling, making the code more modular and easier to manage. The author demonstrates this with a newsletter signup form and an invoice screen, showing how to implement a loading button that can be reused without styling constraints.

recent_posts.title: How to build a Recursive React Component
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to build a recursive React component to render a nested folder structure, such as a file tree. The guide walks through creating a single component that can handle arbitrary levels of nesting by leveraging recursion. It also includes techniques for adding state management, handling TypeScript types, and differentiating between files and folders.

recent_posts.title: Building an Elastic Slider with Framer Motion and Radix
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to transform a basic slider into an advanced interactive component using Framer Motion and Radix. The tutorial includes techniques like micro-interactions on hover, rubber band effects, dynamic icon tracking, and more, all styled with Tailwind CSS. These enhancements mimic the smooth, responsive animations seen in iOS sliders.

recent_posts.title: Optimistic UI in Remix
recent_posts.summary: The post explores how to build optimistic UIs using Remix, focusing on a work journal app. It addresses eliminating pending UI, using 'use Fetchers' to fetch form data globally, managing entries with unique IDs to avoid race conditions, and allowing immediate form field refocus and submission. By utilizing a new Remix API for submissions without navigation and integrating client-side IDs, the solution ensures a responsive UI that syncs effectively with the backend, highlighting the robustness and flexibility of Remix's features.

recent_posts.title: Session cookies in Remix
recent_posts.summary: This post covers how to add authenticated state to a Remix application using session cookies. It explains setting up a login route, creating and managing cookies for storing session data, and safeguarding sessions from tampering with Remix's createCookieSessionStorage API. The tutorial includes step-by-step instructions and best practices for secure session handling. There is also information about an early bird sale for the course with additional content on build UI.

recent_posts.title: What is Radix Themes?
recent_posts.summary: Radix Themes provides a set of professionally designed UI components for React, including tables, forms, dropdowns, and dialogues. It allows for easy customization to match your application's brand or style. Users can modify accent colors, switch between light and dark modes, and adjust components' appearance through a central theme component. All design elements are crafted to work seamlessly together, enhancing consistency and accessibility across the app.

recent_posts.title: 6 New Tailwind Techniques in 8 minutes
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses various advanced Tailwind CSS techniques such as using the 'accent' utility for consistent styling, applying arbitrary value syntax for dynamic text sizing, balancing text with the 'balance' utility, using the ':has' pseudo-class for parent/child relationships, and leveraging container queries for responsive design. Additionally, it showcases the use of CSS grid's masonry layout for better responsive designs.

top_posts.title: 6 ideas for animating your app with Framer Motion
top_posts.summary: Discover six key concepts for animating your app with Framer Motion, demonstrated through six different demos. The video explains how to animate SVGs, create exit animations, utilize scroll primitives, implement a full-screen carousel, resize panels dynamically, and build an infinite scrollable calendar. Each demo highlights a specific API or method in Framer Motion, offering insights into making efficient and engaging animations for your applications.
